exorcist.direction: Calm, authoritative, dry, concise; never theatrical.

lines.text: At last. I was beginning to think no one would notice the bell.
You saw the pattern. That will have to be enough.

ghost.direction: Adult supernatural voice; controlled, intimate and cold rather than theatrical. Anger surfaces only when the exorcist seals it.

lines.text: So the bell still remembers me.
lines.generationText: [distant, hollow, drawing closer] So… the bell still remembers me.

lines.text: You should have listened when the footsteps stopped.
lines.generationText: [softly, close behind the listener] You should have listened when the footsteps stopped.

lines.text: Don't be afraid. The house keeps what the village gives it.
lines.generationText: [almost comforting, with quiet hunger] Don't be afraid. The house keeps what the village gives it.

lines.text: At last… you opened the wrong cage.
lines.generationText: [relieved, darkly satisfied] At last… you opened the wrong cage.

lines.text: Another name for the house. Our bargain holds.
lines.generationText: [calm, with layered resonance] Another name for the house. Our bargain holds.

lines.text: You… you again. Even death could not teach you to leave me buried.
lines.generationText: [stunned to recognize an old enemy, then filling with bitter, wounded hatred] You… you again. Even death could not teach you to leave me buried.

lines.text: No—no, NO! You cannot bind me to their silence again!
lines.generationText: [panicked, speaking quickly and struggling as an unseen force drags the voice away] No—no, NO! You cannot bind me to their silence again!

kid.audioDecision: The four required lines use a suitable existing ElevenLabs Voice Library voice. Voice Design remained unused after its child-character prompts were blocked. Optional lines remain text-only, and all supernatural speech belongs to the adult ghost.
kid.direction: Natural, curious and slightly uneasy; never threatening. Possession speech always switches to the adult ghost.

lines.text: You're the new tenant. I wondered when you'd arrive.
You haven't gone inside yet?
Are you waiting for something?
If you hear walking after dark, don't answer the door.
I used to go inside. I don't anymore.
You should ask the chief. He knows more about it.
It watches me every day. I don't think it likes what it sees.
It was digging at the wall again, wasn't it?
Maybe it's waiting for me to understand.
It's quiet. I don't think I've ever heard it this quiet.

nonSpokenEvents.text: The kid recoils as the bell rings. A tall adult shadow rises behind them.

chief.direction: Polite, controlled, intelligent and morally ambiguous; suspicion emerges gradually.

lines.text: Ah—you must be the new tenant. Your room is ready. The house is just up the path.
lines.generationText: [pleasantly surprised] Ah—you must be the new tenant. [reassuring] Your room is ready. [quietly amused] The house is just up the path.

lines.text: Ah… another tenant. The house has been prepared again. You may go up whenever you're ready.
lines.generationText: [pleasantly surprised] Ah… another tenant. [quietly pleased] The house has been prepared again. [brightly, ushering them onward] You may go up whenever you're ready.

lines.text: I trust you found everything you need.
The house is waiting. You should settle in before dark.
Travellers rarely stay long. I've learned not to ask where the road takes them next.
lines.generationText: [lightly dismissive] Travellers rarely stay long. [chuckles softly] [with playful indifference] I've learned not to ask where the road takes them next.

lines.text: They left before dawn. That is all I can tell you.
You should concern yourself with your own stay.
Old houses make old sounds. You'll find it comfortable once you stop listening to every creak.
lines.generationText: [reassuringly] Old houses make old sounds. [chuckles softly] [gently teasing] You'll find it comfortable… once you stop listening to every creak.

lines.text: A little wind gets beneath the doors. Nothing more.
You'll understand once you've spent a night there.
That creature? A stray—with an unfortunate interest in that wall.
lines.generationText: [dismissively] That creature? [dryly amused] A stray—with an unfortunate interest in that wall.

lines.text: It has been digging there for days. It never finds anything.
Leave it alone. It will move when it tires.
Put that away. Some things are buried because they should remain forgotten.
lines.generationText: [startled, suddenly alarmed] Put that AWAY! [breathes in, regaining composure] [low and firm] Some things are buried… because they should remain forgotten.

lines.text: Ah… I had hoped you would simply go to sleep. Give me the key.
lines.generationText: [quietly disappointed] Ah… I had hoped you would simply go to sleep. [tone hardens] Give me the key.

lines.text: What have you done? You have saved yourself. Do not mistake that for saving anyone else.
lines.generationText: [stunned, under his breath] What have you done? [brief pause] [coldly, regaining control] You have saved yourself. [with restrained contempt] Do not mistake that… for saving anyone else.
